text:
sam: Heads up — seeing sustained NVMe temps on gnode-eu-west2 racks 5-7. Drives hitting 85-86C, throughput collapsing, GPU pods Pending with DiskPressure. IOPS reported ~3k where baseline is 50k. Logs/snippet below:

sam: ```
= iostat -x 1 3 (nvme0n1)
Device:         rrqm/s wrqm/s   r/s   w/s  rMB/s  wMB/s avgrq-sz avgqu-sz await r_await w_await svctm %util
nvme0n1           0.00  10.00  5.00 50.00   0.20   1.00    24.00    8.50  45.00  10.00  50.00  2.20  66.00
```

sam: smartctl shows rising temperature and increased reallocation events: "Reallocated_Sector_Ct" bumping on some drives. Not full ECC corruption yet but worried about thermal throttling.

june: :eyes: which node pool id? tags?

sam: gnode-eu-west2-gpu-pool-2 (spot-preemptible). Affected nodes: gn-5[2-6]. Firmware NVMe model: PhxFlashX200.

alex: those drives are new gen but have tighter thermal envelope. Could be airflow in that rack or the local scrub/trim schedule overlapping heavy GPU batch windows.

sasha: any scrubbers / background maintenance kicked off? I saw increased ephemeral-scrub activity last night in the job logs.

sam: infra-bot: scrub-runner triggered on gn-520 at 03:12 UTC (auto).

infra-bot: "auto-scrub started on gn-520 (reason: age>30d). Estimated IO load: medium-high."

mike: If scrubs + GPU batching + high ambient datacenter temp = thermal and IOPS collapse. We should avoid scrubs during peak scheduling.

oncall: I'm paged, looking. Quick mitigation: cordon affected nodes and move new node provisioning to other racks.

june: plan: 1) cordon gn-522..gn-526 now. 2) disable auto-scrub for that pool for 2h. 3) rotate workloads to cold racks. 4) collect SMART dump for 6 drives, open ticket with vendor if reallocation continues.

alex: agree. Also consider lowering scrub concurrency and switch to low-io pattern: "--io-limits 100mbps --parallel 1" for that pool.

sam: doing commands now:

sam: ```
kubectl cordon gn-522 gn-523 gn-524 gn-525 gn-526 -n gpu-cluster
kubectl drain gn-522 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data -n gpu-cluster || true
/tooling/ephemeral-cleaner set --pool gnode-eu-west2-gpu-pool-2 --auto-scrub off --until 2475304700
```

mike: also patching node agent to report temperature as a metric to infra prometheus with 30s granularity (currently 5m). Will push a hotfix.

infra-bot: "drain job started for gn-522 (job id: 8843). Estimated evict time 6m/pod."

june: we need a medium-term action: either replace PhxFlashX200 in that rack with drives rated for high-temp, or adjust scheduling so GPU batch jobs avoid those racks during warm months. Capex vs scheduler change. Thoughts?

alex: replacing drives across fleet is expensive. Short term highlight: avoid scheduling heavy seq-len inference that causes sustained write bursts to local scratch on those nodes. Use remote scratch (s3fs/rclone) where latency is less important.

mike: cost calc quick note: replacing 20 drives in that cluster ~ $28k + swap ops. Scheduler change + IOQoS to defer scrubs ~ operational cost (engineering time) but cheaper.

sasha: can we enable IOQoS at node level to cap scrub/io to 10k iops per nvme and prioritize pod io? Linux blkcg + cfq tweaks maybe. Might be lower risk than hardware swap.

june: action items:
- sam: collect full SMART dumps, attach to ticket (owner: sam) — due in 2h
- mike: push prometheus temp metric hotfix + alert (owner: mike) — 1h
- alex: patch scrub-runner to backoff based on node temp + current iops (owner: alex) — 4h
- sasha: prototype blkio QoS psuedo-config and test in staging (owner: sasha) — today EOD
- oncall: keep nodes cordoned until we confirm stable (owner: oncall) — ongoing

oncall: temporary mitigations applied, will monitor. If reallocation_count increases we escalate vendor support.

sam: smart dumps attached to ticket #INF-4321 (link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-4321). Reallocation_count incremented by 2 on gn-524.

june: good catch. keep an eye on %util and avgq. If %util stays >70% under normal load we need immediate reprovision to other AZs.

mike: logging note for postmortem: we didn't have temp-triggered backoff in scrub-runner. Add to infra reliability backlog.

alex: small follow — for customers on Dedicated, this is a data point to justify moving hot scratch to ephemeral that is provisioned with thermal-friendly drives. I'll draft a short ops note.

sasha: :thumbsup: I'll start blkio PoC now and post results here.

oncall: monitoring: added alert rule "nvme_temp_high AND nvme_iops_drop" -> paging to eng-infra-oncall. Threshold: temp>80C for 5m AND iops<10k relative baseline 30% drop.

sam: thanks all. Nodes stable for now, temps trending down after drains. Closing follow-ups in ticket.

june: keeping this thread pinned until next update.

sam: FYI — learned: PhxFlashX200 has aggressive thermal throttling after sustained 80s. Vendor advised firmware 2.1.7 fixes some behavior — vendor ticket opened.
